content:
incident-bot: PAGER: hosted-prod-eu provisioner backfill lag > 5m, GPU pool utilization 100% (eu-hosted-gpu). queue_depth=7200, ingress-rate spike detected from partner 'alpha-integration'. auto-scale attempts failing with quota errors. paging on-call SRE. :rotating_light:

maya: on it. pulling metrics now. can someone drop the recent deploy diff?

jordan: not me, I was on docs deploy. no new infra deploys in last 30m.

maya: checking autoscaler logs -> saw repeated 403 from cloud API when requesting new instances: 
```
error: quotaExceeded: project has insufficient GPU quota for zone europe-west1
```

adam: confirmed. cloud quota enforcement kicked in across eu zones 3m ago. looks like alpha-integration ramped from 200 -> 5k req/s in 90s.

sara: p95/p99 for hosted-api-eu now: p95=1.8s (baseline 120ms), p99=12.4s, timeouts started at ~1768205600. customers seeing 504s.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling back canary is a manual action, no active canary flagged.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) immediate soft rate-limits on partner key; 2) enable model-fallback for non-enterprise tenants (small-quant) to reduce GPU usage; 3) attempt cross-region fallback to us-west; 4) open quota request — but that is slow. executing 1 now.

jordan: +1. how do we implement soft qps? can we push a quick route-level cap?

maya: doing it now: 
```
rictl routes update --name alpha-integration --rate-limit 20rps --duration 10m
```

maya: rate-limit applied. hitting partner with 429 now. queue inflow dropping. ingress-rate down from 5k -> 1.2k rps. queue depth falling to ~4800.

adam: pushing fallback rules to routing: non-enterprise keys will map to model: 'gpt-medium-quant' instead of 'gpt-large' for 15m. this should cut average GPU time per request by ~3x.

jordan: command: 
```
rictl routing set-fallback --selector "tier!=enterprise" --model gpt-medium-quant --ttl 900
```

ops-bot: autoscaler: attempted nodes +4 -> failed: quotaExceeded; attempted fallback zone eu-west2 -> succeeded partially (launched 1 node).

maya: spinning up dedicated fallback: requesting immediate lane on dedicated pool eu-ded-1 for critical customers. starting transfer of enterprise tokens to dedicated pool.

customer-success: CS note: alpha-integration is a partner sending heavy demo traffic for new feature. they have some paid customers hit. I'm pinging their PM to throttle.

adam: metric note: CPU on provisioners also spiked due to KV-cache misses when models changed. enabling caching sticky-session to reduce churn.

leo: any ETA on queue drain / customer impact?

sara: p95 improved to 800ms after rate-limit & fallback. p99 down to 5.6s. queue depth 4800 -> 2100 in last 6m. error rate (504) trending down from 6% -> 1.2%.

maya: switching live dashboards to incident view, attaching logs. 

incident-bot: NOTE: escalation policy invoked: Eng on-call Jordan to assist with provisioning and routing.

jordan: I'm checking cross-region routing; found one misconfiguration where eu route priorities favored local capacity even when saturated. updating policy to allow us-west fallback for alpha-integration only.

jordan: updated. traffic shift beginning (~10% moving to us-west). latency for those requests ~420ms (extra RTT). overall p95 now 650ms.

ops-bot: audit log: 
```
[1768205621] route-update alpha-integration rate-limit 20rps by maya
[1768205660] routing-fallback set by adam
[1768205720] autoscaler attempted 4 nodes -> quotaExceeded
[1768205783] node launched in eu-west2 (1 of 4)
```

maya: quick customer impact summary for postmortem: - impacted tenants: alpha-integration and any small-volume customers on same pool; - observed peak queue depth: 7200; - peak p99: 12.4s; - approx 14% of requests returned 504 at peak; - root cause: sudden external fanout + exhausted GPU quota preventing autoscaler from meeting demand.

customer-success: FYI, I've told alpha PM to pause demo traffic for 20m and will coordinate a retro. They acknowledged and paused at 1768206000.

adam: manual intervention: increased per-tenant concurrency limits for enterprise keys on dedicated pool to relieve SLAs during migration: 
```
rictl pool migrate-tokens --from eu-hosted-gpu --to eu-ded-1 --tokens-file enterprise_tokens.txt
```

maya: migration in progress. 85% enterprise tokens moved. dedicated pool absorbing ~300 rps.

leo: any risk of repeated surge? can we add defensive throttles globally?

jordan: enabling short global backpressure: token bucket with 80% throttle cross-tenant for 10m to prevent exhaustion.

mana (typo correction): (ignore)

ops-bot: incident timeline marker added.

maya: final status check: queue depth steady at 420, p95=210ms, p99=480ms, error rate < 0.2%. partner paused. autoscaler still showing quota errors if asked for >1 nodes. we've created a high-priority quota ticket with cloud support (ref: Q-987654).

jordan: handing off to overnight oncall SRE Adam for watch & follow-ups. Adam, please confirm you have runbook steps and that CS has communicated with partner.

adam: taking handoff. I've documented mitigations in the runbook channel and set reminder to check quota response at 1768209000. CS confirmed partner paused. will watch for retry waves.

customer-success: I'll follow up with alpha PM at 1768207000 for formal note and to collect log slices for their team.

maya: closing active mitigation. leaving temporary routing + rate-limits in place for 20m. please file incident ticket with root cause, timeline, and cost impact.

ops-bot: incident resolved -> status: mitigated. reopen if queue rises >1000 or p99 > 1s.

adam: postmortem owners: maya (lead), jordan (routing), sara (monitoring), customer-success (stakeholder comms).

maya: thanks all. nice quick coordination. :thumbsup:

---

(Notes to postmortem: include exact autoscaler error logs, cloud quota request timeline, partner traffic pattern, suggestions: per-client burst limits, proactive quota headroom, cross-region fallback priority tests, and automated move-to-dedicated policy when enterprise tokens exceed threshold)
